source: Ideal-gas Cp: a degree-5 fit in (T - 298.15 K), through its 273.16 K value, to the ideal-gas Cp of CoolProp Nitrogen.json EOS[0].alpha0 (Span et al. 2000; CoolProp 8.0.0 (github.com/CoolProp/CoolProp ae81610e, MIT)), 273.16..900 K, worst 0.011 %; below 273.16 K the heat capacity is held at its 273.16 K value, 29.116 J/(mol K), within 0.05 % of the same ideal-gas Cp down to the triple point (owner decision D37, simplification S4). Viscosity: the CoolProp 8.0.0 tables of properties/pilot_nitrogen.json (Lemmon and Jacobsen 2004). PR constants from CoolProp. Nitrogen cross-interactions initially estimated zero. Built by tools/open-thermo-data/derive.mjs (batch 2026-11-04-open-thermo-data, O2).

fluid_domain.evidence: Nitrogen triple point 63.151 K (Span et al. 2000) to 900 K. Validated in F4 (FluidNitrogenCryogenicTest, references from the Span et al. 2000 equation of state in CoolProp 8.0.0 since batch 2026-11-04-open-thermo-data): ideal-gas Cp below 273.16 K (the fit's value there, held) within 0.05 % of the zero-pressure Cp; vapour Cp at 100 K and 200 K, 1 atm, within 1 %; viscosity tables cover the temperature range. Every phase at its own pressure (P3 WP4): PR78 saturation pressure at 77.355 K +1.21 %, saturated liquid density -0.07 %; compressed liquid to 10 MPa within 0.19, 0.34, 1.15 % of the Helmholtz reference at Tr 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 (3.55 % at Tr 0.9) and -0.17 % at 77.36 K, 10 MPa (DirectLiquidContinuityTest; P1 study). 10 MPa per P3 design section 8.1: the declared critical band (Tr 0.95-1.1 x Pr 0.8-1.5, 119.9-138.8 K x 2.72-5.09 MPa, and the plan's two smaller boxes) is research-only, typed by the equilibrium engine (P3 WP7). Viscosity above 2 MPa for dense states is a reference-pressure value.

freezing.source: ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Nitrogen" (ChemSep index 905, CAS 7727-37-9): melting point, triple point temperature and pressure, heat of fusion at the melting point. Data only: never a validity floor or a range end.

thermochemistry.source: 0 by definition: N2 is an element in its reference state (ChemSep agrees). Ideal-gas heat of formation at 298.15 K and formula N2 (molar mass 28.014 g/mol) of ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Nitrogen" (ChemSep index 905, CAS 7727-37-9). Heats of reaction follow by Hess's law. Data only.

combustion.source: Hess's law on this record's thermochemistry (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1): the formula burnt to CO2, H2O (gas), SO2 and N2 on the ideal-gas heats of formation at 298.15 K of icheme:chemsep_carbon_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1), icheme:water (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1) and icheme:chemsep_sulfur_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1). Gives no heat. Computed by tools/heating-values/heating-values.mjs. Read by a fired heater's burners.

eppr78-2022.source: PPR78 group counts of ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Nitrogen" (ChemSep index 905, CAS 7727-37-9), group numbers mapped to the names of the eppr78-2022 group_interactions record (eppr78-2022-si-table-s4-r2). Data for the pairs derived from group counts.

henry_in_water.source: IAPWS G7-04, Guideline on the Henry's Constant and Vapor-Liquid Distribution Constant for Gases in H2O and D2O at High Temperatures (2004), after R. Fernandez-Prini, J. L. Alvarez, A. H. Harvey, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 32 (2003) 903, table of A, B, C for N2 in H2O: ln(kH/p*) = A/Tr + B tau^0.355/Tr + C Tr^-0.41 exp(tau), Tr = T/647.096 K, tau = 1 - Tr, p* the saturation pressure of water, kH on the mole-fraction basis. Coefficients as in Table 2 of the guideline (iapws.org, read 2026-11-11). Copyright 2004 IAPWS; publication in whole or in part is allowed provided attribution is given to IAPWS.

liquid.source: CoolProp 8.0.0 HEOS saturated-liquid viscosity (Q = 0), Lemmon and Jacobsen (2004), Int. J. Thermophys. 25, 21 via the Nitrogen.json transport block, from the triple point to the critical temperature; log-linear interpolation within 0.049 % of CoolProp everywhere but the last 0.0010 K below the critical point (0.56 % there). Saturation-pressure (reference-pressure) approximation: no pressure dependence.

vapor.source: CoolProp 8.0.0 HEOS zero-density viscosity (evaluated at 1e-6 mol/m3), Lemmon and Jacobsen (2004), Int. J. Thermophys. 25, 21, from the triple point to 1200 K; log-linear interpolation within 0.048 % of CoolProp. The pressure fields name the network's minimum pressure at which the table is read (reference-pressure approximation).
